source.name: SECOM
source.citation: McCann, M. & Johnston, A. (2008). SECOM [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C54305
source.note: The raw files are not committed; ml/real/download_secom.py fetches them. This file contains derived results and the readings of the 8 charted sensors, shared under the same licence with credit.

spc.selection: 8 sensors at evenly spaced positions among 301 sensors with <5% missing and >=100 distinct values in the baseline window; no label used
spc.chart: individuals (limits = baseline mean +/- 3 x mean moving range / 1.128, held fixed)

rules.WE2: 2 of 3 points beyond 2 sigma, same side
rules.WE3: 4 of 5 points beyond 1 sigma, same side
rules.WE4: 8 points in a row on one side of the centre line
rules.N5: 6 points in a row steadily rising or falling
rules.N6: 14 points in a row alternating up and down

capability.reason: Sensors are anonymized and the dataset publishes no specification limits, so there is no defensible LSL or USL. Cpk and Ppk would need an invented spec, and inventing one would make the number meaningless. Only control-chart behaviour is reported.

protocol.split: by time: the first 1096 runs train, the last 471 runs test
protocol.tuning: 5-fold time-ordered cross-validation (expanding window) inside the training period, scored on PR-AUC
protocol.threshold: chosen to maximise F1 on out-of-fold training predictions, then applied unchanged to the test period
protocol.test_set_used: once, after all fitting, tuning and threshold choice
protocol.missing_values: filled with training-period medians; sensors constant in training are dropped

majority_class.note: Predicts pass for every run. It flags nothing, so precision is undefined and recall is 0.

control_chart_rule.rule: flag a run if any of the top 5 sensors is beyond 3 sigma of its baseline limits; the 5 sensors are those whose training-period values best separate fail from pass

bridge.definition: a failure is flagged if any charted sensor gave a signal at that run or in the 5 runs before it (about 7 hours at about 18 runs a day); passing runs are scored the same way, so the share of passes flagged is the false-alarm base rate
